dedupe_keys.name: stochastic geometry model of infrastructure sharing between mobile network operators with a cournot market

description: This paper models infrastructure sharing among mobile network operators, with one buyer operator and several sellers, as a way to cut costs and use existing network resources better. Modelling base station locations as a homogeneous Poisson point process, it derives the downlink SINR coverage probability for a buyer's user, analyses the trade-off between raising transmit power and raising base station intensity to meet a coverage target, shows that a seller's areal power consumption is a piecewise function of intensity, and then formulates a single-buyer multiple-seller market in which sellers set prices and shares of infrastructure to sell as a Cournot oligopoly, proving that iterative best responses converge to the Nash equilibrium. Producer: Sanguanpuak, Guruacharya, Hossain, Rajatheva and Latva-aho; the arXiv abstract page shows submission on 23 September 2017. Coverage: a generic analytical model. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; no code was mentioned. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: an analytical model with idealised Poisson deployments, not calibrated to a real operator. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning and optimisation of shared radio access deployments and their pricing. Related record: the techno-economic assessment of rural 5G infrastructure sharing (case_study-rural-5g-infrastructure-sharing-techno-economic).
